sanskrit: gatotsavaṃ puram iva hṛtanāgam iva hradam strīvarṣavarabhūyiṣṭhaṃ vṛddhāmātyair adhiṣṭhitam
english: It was like a city whose festival had ended, like a pool from which the elephant had been carried off—thronged for the most part with women, and watched over by aged ministers.

sanskrit: tatraitān paryupātiṣṭhan duryodhanapuraḥsarāḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭā rājan kāṣāyamalināmbarāḥ
english: There, O king, those who had once gone before Duryodhana waited upon them, their palms joined in supplication, clad in soiled ochre garments.

sanskrit: śibiraṃ samanuprāpya kururājasya pāṇḍavāḥ avaterur mahārāja rathebhyo rathasattamāḥ
english: Having reached the camp of the Kuru king, the Pāṇḍavas, those foremost of chariot-warriors, descended from their chariots, O great king.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvadhanvānam abhyabhāṣata keśavaḥ sthitaḥ priyahite nityam atīva bharatarṣabha
english: Then Keśava, ever devoted to his welfare and his good, addressed the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: avaropaya gāṇḍīvam akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī athāham avarokṣyāmi paścād bharatasattama
english: "Lay down the Gāṇḍīva and the two inexhaustible great quivers; afterward I too shall descend, O best of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: svayaṃ caivāvaroha tvam etac chreyas tavānagha tac cākarot tathā vīraḥ pāṇḍuputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "And do you yourself dismount; this is for your good, O blameless one." And so the hero Dhanaṃjaya, son of Pāṇḍu, did just that.

sanskrit: atha paścāt tataḥ kṛṣṇo raśmīn utsṛjya vājinām avārohata medhāvī rathād gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: Then afterward the wise Kṛṣṇa, releasing the reins of the horses, descended from the chariot of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: athāvatīrṇe bhūtānām īśvare sumahātmani kapir antardadhe divyo dhvajo gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: And when the lord of beings, that great-souled one, had stepped down, the divine ape-banner of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva vanished from sight.

sanskrit: sa dagdho droṇakarṇābhyāṃ divyair astrair mahārathaḥ atha dīpto 'gninā hy āśu prajajvāla mahīpate
english: That mighty chariot, scorched by Droṇa and Karṇa with their divine weapons, then, kindled by fire, blazed up at once, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: sopāsaṅgaḥ saraśmiś ca sāśvaḥ sayugabandhuraḥ bhasmībhūto 'patad bhūmau ratho gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: With its quivers, its reins, its horses, its yoke and chariot-pole, the chariot of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, reduced to ashes, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā bhasmabhūtaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍusutāḥ prabho abhavan vismitā rājann arjunaś cedam abravīt
english: Seeing it thus turned to ashes, the sons of Pāṇḍu were filled with wonder, O lord; and Arjuna, O king, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kṛtāñjaliḥ sapraṇayaṃ praṇipatyābhivādya ca govinda kasmād bhagavan ratho dagdho 'yam agninā
english: With joined palms, affectionately bowing down and saluting him: "Govinda, blessed lord, why was this chariot consumed by fire?"

sanskrit: kim etan mahad āścaryam abhavad yadunandana tan me brūhi mahābāho śrotavyaṃ yadi manyase
english: "What is this great marvel that has come to pass, O delight of the Yadus? Tell me of it, mighty-armed one, if you deem it fit for me to hear."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca astrair bahuvidhair dagdhaḥ pūrvam evāyam arjuna madadhiṣṭhitatvāt samare na viśīrṇaḥ paraṃtapa
english: Vāsudeva said: This chariot had already been burned by weapons of many kinds, O Arjuna; yet because I occupied it, it did not break apart in battle, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: idānīṃ tu viśīrṇo 'yaṃ dagdho brahmāstratejasā mayā vimuktaḥ kaunteya tvayy adya kṛtakarmaṇi
english: But now, scorched by the fiery power of the Brahmā-weapon, it has crumbled, for I have released it today, O son of Kuntī, now that your task is accomplished.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca īṣad utsmayamānaś ca bhagavān keśavo 'rihā pariṣvajya ca rājānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: And the blessed Keśava, slayer of foes, smiling faintly, embraced King Yudhiṣṭhira and spoke to him.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jayasi kaunteya diṣṭyā te śatravo jitāḥ diṣṭyā gāṇḍīvadhanvā ca bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "By good fortune you are victorious, O son of Kuntī; by good fortune your foes are conquered; by good fortune the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava are well."

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi kuśalī rājan mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau muktā vīrakṣayād asmāt saṃgrāmān nihatadviṣaḥ kṣipram uttarakālāni kuru kāryāṇi bhārata
english: "And you too are safe, O king, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī; delivered from this slaughter of heroes, your enemies slain, swiftly perform the rites that now remain to be done, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: upayātam upaplavyaṃ saha gāṇḍīvadhanvanā ānīya madhuparkaṃ māṃ yat purā tvam avocathāḥ
english: "When I came to Upaplavya together with the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, and you brought me the honey-offering, what you then said to me—"

sanskrit: eṣa bhrātā sakhā caiva tava kṛṣṇa dhanaṃjayaḥ rakṣitavyo mahābāho sarvāsv āpatsv iti prabho tava caivaṃ bruvāṇasya tathety evāham abruvam
english: "'This Dhanaṃjaya is your brother and your friend, O Kṛṣṇa; he is to be guarded, mighty-armed one, in every peril, O lord'—and to you who spoke thus I answered, 'So be it.'"

sanskrit: sa savyasācī guptas te vijayī ca nareśvara bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rājendra śūraḥ satyaparākramaḥ mukto vīrakṣayād asmāt saṃgrāmād romaharṣaṇāt
english: "That ambidextrous archer has been guarded for you and is victorious, O lord of men; together with his brothers, O king of kings, that valiant one of truthful prowess is delivered from this slaughter of heroes, from this hair-raising battle."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kṛṣṇena dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ hṛṣṭaromā mahārāja pratyuvāca janārdanam
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, the hair of his body bristling with joy, O great king, replied to Janārdana.

sanskrit: pramuktaṃ droṇakarṇābhyāṃ brahmāstram arimardana kas tvad anyaḥ sahet sākṣād api vajrī puraṃdaraḥ
english: "The Brahmā-weapon let loose by Droṇa and by Karṇa, O crusher of foes—who other than you could withstand it, even Purandara the wielder of the thunderbolt in person?"

sanskrit: bhavatas tu prasādena saṃgrāme bahavo jitāḥ mahāraṇagataḥ pārtho yac ca nāsīt parāṅmukhaḥ
english: "By your grace many have been conquered in battle, and Pārtha, plunged into the great fray, never turned his face away."

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahābāho paryāyair bahubhir mayā karmaṇām anusaṃtānaṃ tejasaś ca gatiḥ śubhā
english: "And likewise, mighty-armed one, through many turns of fortune I have seen the unbroken succession of deeds and the auspicious course of your splendor."

sanskrit: upaplavye maharṣir me kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt yato dharmas tataḥ kṛṣṇo yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ
english: "At Upaplavya the great sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana said to me: 'Where there is righteousness, there is Kṛṣṇa; where Kṛṣṇa is, there is victory.'"

sanskrit: ity evam ukte te vīrāḥ śibiraṃ tava bhārata praviśya pratyapadyanta kośaratnarddhisaṃcayān
english: When this had been said, those heroes, having entered your camp, O Bhārata, took possession of the stores of treasure, jewels, and riches.

sanskrit: rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ ca maṇīn atha ca mauktikān bhūṣaṇāny atha mukhyāni kambalāny ajināni ca dāsīdāsam asaṃkhyeyaṃ rājyopakaraṇāni ca
english: Silver and gold, gems and pearls, the finest ornaments, woolen blankets and deerskins, slave-women and slaves beyond counting, and the appurtenances of kingship.

sanskrit: te prāpya dhanam akṣayyaṃ tvadīyaṃ bharatarṣabha udakrośan maheṣvāsā narendra vijitārayaḥ
english: Having obtained your inexhaustible wealth, O bull of the Bhāratas, those great archers, their foes conquered, raised a shout of triumph, O lord of men.

sanskrit: te tu vīrāḥ samāśvasya vāhanāny avamucya ca atiṣṭhanta muhuḥ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ sātyakis tathā
english: Then those heroes, having taken rest and unyoked their mounts, halted there awhile—all the Pāṇḍavas, and Sātyaki likewise.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahārāja vāsudevo mahāyaśāḥ asmābhir maṅgalārthāya vastavyaṃ śibirād bahiḥ
english: Then, O great king, the illustrious Vāsudeva said: "For the sake of auspiciousness we must lodge outside the camp."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā ca te sarve pāṇḍavāḥ sātyakis tathā vāsudevena sahitā maṅgalārthaṃ yayur bahiḥ
english: Saying "So be it," all the Pāṇḍavas, and Sātyaki as well, together with Vāsudeva, went outside for the sake of auspiciousness.

sanskrit: te samāsādya saritaṃ puṇyāmoghavatīṃ nṛpa nyavasann atha tāṃ rātriṃ pāṇḍavā hataśatravaḥ
english: Reaching the holy river Oghavatī, O king, the Pāṇḍavas, their enemies slain, passed that night there.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayām āsur yādavaṃ nāgasāhvayam sa ca prāyāj javenāśu vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān dārukaṃ ratham āropya yena rājāmbikāsutaḥ
english: Then they dispatched the Yādava to the city named after the elephant; and the mighty Vāsudeva, mounting Dāruka upon his chariot, set out swiftly with all speed toward where the king, son of Ambikā, was.

sanskrit: tam ūcuḥ saṃprayāsyantaṃ sainyasugrīvavāhanam pratyāśvāsaya gāndhārīṃ hataputrāṃ yaśasvinīm
english: As he was about to set forth, his steeds Sainya and Sugrīva yoked, they said to him: "Console Gāndhārī, the illustrious lady whose sons are slain."

sanskrit: sa prāyāt pāṇḍavair uktas tat puraṃ sātvatāṃ varaḥ āsasādayiṣuḥ kṣipraṃ gāndhārīṃ nihatātmajām
english: Bidden by the Pāṇḍavas, that best of the Sātvatas set out for that city, eager to reach without delay Gāndhārī, whose sons had been slain.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ rājaśārdūlo dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ gāndhāryāḥ preṣayām āsa vāsudevaṃ paraṃtapam
english: Janamejaya said: For what reason did that tiger among kings, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, send Vāsudeva, scorcher of foes, to Gāndhārī?

sanskrit: yadā pūrvaṃ gataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śamārthaṃ kauravān prati na ca taṃ labdhavān kāmaṃ tato yuddham abhūd idam
english: When Kṛṣṇa had earlier gone for the sake of peace to the Kauravas and had not won that desire, then this war came to pass.

sanskrit: nihateṣu tu yodheṣu hate duryodhane tathā pṛthivyāṃ pāṇḍaveyasya niḥsapatne kṛte yudhi
english: But now that the warriors were slain and Duryodhana likewise killed, and the earth made rivalless for the son of Pāṇḍu by the war,

sanskrit: vidrute śibire śūnye prāpte yaśasi cottame kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ brahman yena kṛṣṇo gataḥ punaḥ
english: the camp scattered and emptied, and the highest glory attained—what then was the reason, O brāhmaṇa, for which Kṛṣṇa went forth once more?

sanskrit: na caitat kāraṇaṃ brahmann alpaṃ vai pratibhāti me yatrāgamad ameyātmā svayam eva janārdanaḥ
english: And this reason does not seem to me a small one, O brāhmaṇa, since the immeasurable Janārdana himself went there in person.

sanskrit: tattvato vai samācakṣva sarvam adhvaryusattama yac cātra kāraṇaṃ brahman kāryasyāsya viniścaye
english: Recount it all to me truly, O best of officiating priests—the reason, O brāhmaṇa, that determined this undertaking.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno yan māṃ pṛcchasi pārthiva tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yathāvad bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: This further question that you ask of me is worthy of you, O prince; I shall declare it to you duly, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: hataṃ duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena saṃyuge vyutkramya samayaṃ rājan dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahābalam
english: Seeing Duryodhana, the mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, slain by Bhīmasena in the duel in transgression of the agreed rule, O king—

sanskrit: anyāyena hataṃ dṛṣṭvā gadāyuddhena bhārata yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahārāja mahad bhayam athāviśat
english: seeing him slain unfairly in the mace-combat, O Bhārata, a great fear then entered Yudhiṣṭhira, O great king.

sanskrit: cintayāno mahābhāgāṃ gāndhārīṃ tapasānvitām ghoreṇa tapasā yuktāṃ trailokyam api sā dahet
english: For he thought of the illustrious Gāndhārī, endowed with austerity—armed with dreadful penance, she could burn even the three worlds.

sanskrit: tasya cintayamānasya buddhiḥ samabhavat tadā gāndhāryāḥ krodhadīptāyāḥ pūrvaṃ praśamanaṃ bhavet
english: As he pondered, this thought then arose in him: the wrath of Gāndhārī, blazing with anger, must first be pacified.

sanskrit: sā hi putravadhaṃ śrutvā kṛtam asmābhir īdṛśam mānasenāgninā kruddhā bhasmasān naḥ kariṣyati
english: "For she, hearing of such a slaying of her sons as we have wrought, will in her wrath reduce us to ashes with the fire of her mind."

sanskrit: kathaṃ duḥkham idaṃ tīvraṃ gāndhārī prasahiṣyati śrutvā vinihataṃ putraṃ chalenājihmayodhinam
english: "How will Gāndhārī endure this fierce grief, when she hears that her son, who fought without guile, was killed by a trick?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vicintya bahudhā bhayaśokasamanvitaḥ vāsudevam idaṃ vākyaṃ dharmarājo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having pondered thus in many ways, filled with fear and grief, the Dharma-king addressed these words to Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tava prasādād govinda rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam aprāpyaṃ manasāpīha prāptam asmābhir acyuta
english: "By your grace, Govinda, the kingdom, its thorns destroyed—a thing unattainable even in thought—has here been won by us, O imperishable one."

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ me mahābāho saṃgrāme romaharṣaṇe vimardaḥ sumahān prāptas tvayā yādavanandana
english: "Before my own eyes, mighty-armed one, in that hair-raising battle, a most mighty struggle was undertaken by you, O delight of the Yādavas."

sanskrit: tvayā devāsure yuddhe vadhārtham amaradviṣām yathā sāhyaṃ purā dattaṃ hatāś ca vibudhadviṣaḥ
english: "As of old in the war of the gods and demons you lent your aid for the slaying of the foes of the immortals, and the enemies of the gods were destroyed,"

sanskrit: sāhyaṃ tathā mahābāho dattam asmākam acyuta sārathyena ca vārṣṇeya bhavatā yad dhṛtā vayam
english: "so too, mighty-armed and imperishable one, you lent your aid to us; and by your charioteering, O Vārṣṇeya, we were upheld."

sanskrit: yadi na tvaṃ bhaven nāthaḥ phalgunasya mahāraṇe kathaṃ śakyo raṇe jetuṃ bhaved eṣa balārṇavaḥ
english: "Had you not been Phalguna's protector in the great battle, how could this ocean of armies have been conquered in the fray?"

sanskrit: gadāprahārā vipulāḥ parighaiś cāpi tāḍanam śaktibhir bhiṇḍipālaiś ca tomaraiḥ saparaśvadhaiḥ
english: "Vast blows of maces, and battering with iron bludgeons, with lances, slings, javelins, and battle-axes—"

sanskrit: vācaś ca paruṣāḥ prāptās tvayā hy asmaddhitaiṣiṇā tāś ca te saphalāḥ sarvā hate duryodhane 'cyuta
english: "and harsh words too were endured by you who sought our good; and all these have borne fruit for you, now that Duryodhana is slain, O imperishable one."

sanskrit: gāndhāryā hi mahābāho krodhaṃ budhyasva mādhava sā hi nityaṃ mahābhāgā tapasogreṇa karśitā
english: "Be mindful, mighty-armed Mādhava, of the wrath of Gāndhārī; for that illustrious lady is ever wasted thin by fierce austerity."

sanskrit: putrapautravadhaṃ śrutvā dhruvaṃ naḥ saṃpradhakṣyati tasyāḥ prasādanaṃ vīra prāptakālaṃ mataṃ mama
english: "Hearing of the slaughter of her sons and grandsons, she will surely burn us up; her appeasement, O hero, is in my judgment now timely."

sanskrit: kaś ca tāṃ krodhadīptākṣīṃ putravyasanakarśitām vīkṣituṃ puruṣaḥ śaktas tvām ṛte puruṣottama
english: "And what man, save you, O best of men, is able even to look upon her, her eyes blazing with anger, worn thin by the calamity of her sons?"

sanskrit: tatra me gamanaṃ prāptaṃ rocate tava mādhava gāndhāryāḥ krodhadīptāyāḥ praśamārtham ariṃdama
english: "To me it seems fitting that you go there, O Mādhava, if it please you, to pacify Gāndhārī, who is ablaze with wrath, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kartā vikartā ca lokānāṃ prabhavāpyayaḥ hetukāraṇasaṃyuktair vākyaiḥ kālasamīritaiḥ
english: "For you are the maker and unmaker of the worlds, their origin and dissolution; with words joined to motive and cause and fitted to the occasion,"

sanskrit: kṣipram eva mahāprājña gāndhārīṃ śamayiṣyasi pitāmahaś ca bhagavān kṛṣṇas tatra bhaviṣyati
english: "swiftly, O greatly wise one, will you calm Gāndhārī; and the venerable grandfather Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana too will be there."

sanskrit: sarvathā te mahābāho gāndhāryāḥ krodhanāśanam kartavyaṃ sātvataśreṣṭha pāṇḍavānāṃ hitaiṣiṇā
english: "By every means, mighty-armed best of the Sātvatas, the quelling of Gāndhārī's wrath must be accomplished by you who seek the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: dharmarājasya vacanaṃ śrutvā yadukulodvahaḥ āmantrya dārukaṃ prāha rathaḥ sajjo vidhīyatām
english: Hearing the words of the Dharma-king, the upholder of the Yadu line summoned Dāruka and said: "Let the chariot be made ready."

sanskrit: keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā tvaramāṇo 'tha dārukaḥ nyavedayad rathaṃ sajjaṃ keśavāya mahātmane
english: Hearing the words of Keśava, Dāruka then in haste reported to the great-souled Keśava that the chariot was ready.

sanskrit: taṃ rathaṃ yādavaśreṣṭhaḥ samāruhya paraṃtapaḥ jagāma hāstinapuraṃ tvaritaḥ keśavo vibhuḥ
english: Mounting that chariot, the best of the Yādavas, the scorcher of foes, the all-pervading Keśava, set out in haste for Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyān mahārāja mādhavo bhagavān rathī nāgasāhvayam āsādya praviveśa ca vīryavān
english: Then, O great king, the blessed Mādhava, that chariot-warrior, set forth; and reaching the city named after the elephant, the valiant one entered it.

sanskrit: praviśya nagaraṃ vīro rathaghoṣeṇa nādayan vidito dhṛtarāṣṭrasya so 'vatīrya rathottamāt
english: Entering the city, the hero, making it resound with the thunder of his chariot, and announced to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, descended from his splendid chariot.

sanskrit: abhyagacchad adīnātmā dhṛtarāṣṭraniveśanam pūrvaṃ cābhigataṃ tatra so 'paśyad ṛṣisattamam
english: With undejected spirit he approached the dwelling of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and there he saw the best of sages, who had come before.

sanskrit: pādau prapīḍya kṛṣṇasya rājñaś cāpi janārdanaḥ abhyavādayad avyagro gāndhārīṃ cāpi keśavaḥ
english: Clasping the feet of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana and of the king as well, Janārdana, unperturbed, paid his respects; and Keśava saluted Gāndhārī too.

sanskrit: tatas tu yādavaśreṣṭho dhṛtarāṣṭram adhokṣajaḥ pāṇim ālambya rājñaḥ sa sasvaraṃ praruroda ha
english: Then the best of the Yādavas, Adhokṣaja, taking hold of the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra's hand, wept aloud.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam ivotsṛjya bāṣpaṃ śokasamudbhavam prakṣālya vāriṇā netre ācamya ca yathāvidhi uvāca praśritaṃ vākyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭram ariṃdamaḥ
english: After shedding for a moment the tears born of grief, washing his eyes with water and sipping water as enjoined, the subduer of foes spoke humble words to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid bhūtabhavyasya bhārata kālasya ca yathā vṛttaṃ tat te suviditaṃ prabho
english: "There is nothing of past or future unknown to you, O Bhārata; and how the working of time has come to pass is well known to you, O lord."

sanskrit: yad idaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ sarvais tava cittānurodhibhiḥ kathaṃ kulakṣayo na syāt tathā kṣatrasya bhārata
english: "This was the very thing all the Pāṇḍavas, deferring to your wishes, strove for—that there might be no destruction of the lineage, nor of the warrior class, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā kṣāntavān dharmavatsalaḥ dyūtacchalajitaiḥ śaktair vanavāso 'bhyupāgataḥ
english: "Making a compact with his brothers, that lover of righteousness forbore; defeated by the trickery of the dice though they were able men, he submitted to dwelling in the forest."

sanskrit: ajñātavāsacaryā ca nānāveśasamāvṛtaiḥ anye ca bahavaḥ kleśās tv aśaktair iva nityadā
english: "And the practice of living in concealment, cloaked in various disguises, and many other hardships besides, were borne ever, as though by men without power."

sanskrit: mayā ca svayam āgamya yuddhakāla upasthite sarvalokasya sāṃnidhye grāmāṃs tvaṃ pañca yācitaḥ
english: "And by me, coming in person when the hour of war was at hand, in the presence of all the world, you were asked for five villages."

sanskrit: tvayā kālopasṛṣṭena lobhato nāpavarjitāḥ tavāparādhān nṛpate sarvaṃ kṣatraṃ kṣayaṃ gatam
english: "By you, smitten by time, out of greed they were not granted; and through your fault, O king, the whole warrior race has gone to destruction."

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa somadattena bāhlikena kṛpeṇa ca droṇena ca saputreṇa vidureṇa ca dhīmatā yācitas tvaṃ śamaṃ nityaṃ na ca tat kṛtavān asi
english: "By Bhīṣma, by Somadatta, by Bāhlika and Kṛpa, by Droṇa together with his son, and by the wise Vidura, you were ever entreated for peace; yet you did not make it."
